neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert. Previously disciplined military officer now makes sexually inappropriate comments. Laughs when wife cries about his behavior. MMSE 21/30. FAB 10/18. Category fluency: 7/60 seconds. Severe disinhibition evident throughout. Bilateral frontal release signs.
neurological_exam.additional: Wife reports compulsive behavior — patient rearranges military memorabilia daily for hours.

patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition and personality change in a retired military officer.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F. is a 64-year-old right-handed White retired military officer referred for evaluation of progressive personality change over 2 years. A decorated officer known for his strict discipline and professionalism, he has undergone a dramatic personality transformation. He resigned from his second career in real estate 2 years ago after making a sexual remark to a client. Since then, his behavior has escalated: he makes explicit sexual comments to female neighbors, gets into confrontations at grocery stores, and once exposed himself to family members during a gathering. He has developed compulsive military-themed rituals — rearranging his medals and memorabilia in precise order for hours each day. His appetite has become voracious. His alcohol use has escalated from rare to 4-6 beers daily. He shows complete lack of insight, stating he is 'just more relaxed now.' His wife is terrified and has removed firearms from the home after he made an impulsive comment about shooting a neighbor's dog. No family history of dementia.

additional_observations: Small vessel ischemic disease: scattered periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensities — age-appropriate, no cortical infarcts
mri.impression: Severe bilateral frontal and moderate anterior temporal atrophy with knife-blade pattern. Small vessel ischemic changes are age-appropriate and not the primary etiology. Clinical correlation recommended.

advanced_imaging.impression: Severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism. Posterior cortex spared. Pattern diagnostic of bvFTD. Small vessel ischemic changes do not explain this metabolic pattern.
recommended_actions: Urgent safety planning — firearms must be removed from home

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 130 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 45 mg/dL. Glucose: 62 mg/dL (ratio 0.67). Abeta42: 840 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 220 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 37 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 1,950 pg/mL (elevated). 14-3-3: negative.

results.title: Firearms and dementia
results.finding: People with FTD have markedly increased risk of impulsive, violent behavior; firearms in home represent serious safety hazard

output.summary: Firearms removal is a critical safety intervention in bvFTD given profound impulsivity and disinhibition. Caregiver counseling on safety planning is essential.

differential.key_features: Small vessel changes are age-appropriate, no cortical infarcts, atrophic-predominant pattern on MRI, FDG-PET shows frontotemporal not subcortical pattern
Amyloid PET negative, frontal-predominant, normal hippocampi
Progressive neurodegeneration on imaging rules out purely psychiatric etiology

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Severe bifrontal atrophy; small vessel changes are incidental

optimal_actions.action: IMMEDIATE: Address firearms in home — safety emergency

critical_actions: URGENT: Counsel family about immediate firearms removal from home — impulsivity and disinhibition in bvFTD creates extreme risk
Diagnose bvFTD — classic presentation with severe disinhibition and frontal atrophy/hypometabolism
Do not attribute small vessel ischemic changes on MRI as the primary diagnosis — frontal atrophy pattern and FDG-PET pattern are diagnostic of FTD
contraindicated_actions: Attributing behavioral changes to PTSD or alcohol without neuroimaging
Diagnosing vascular dementia based on incidental small vessel changes
key_reasoning_points: Small vessel ischemic changes are common in 64-year-old with CAD risk factors and are incidental — they do not explain severe personality change and frontal atrophy
Severe bifrontal atrophy with hypometabolism and normal amyloid PET is diagnostic of bvFTD
Firearms safety assessment is a critical clinical responsibility in patients with bvFTD — impulsivity creates extreme danger
Alcohol escalation is symptom of frontal disinhibition, not causative
